merger_description:
Pearson plc, through NCS Pearson, Inc. (**NCS Pearson** and together with Pearson plc, **Pearson**), proposes to acquire Workera Corp (**Workera**) (the **Acquisition**).

Pearson is a global provider of education, assessment and workforce learning products and services. In Australia, Pearson supplies educational content, digital learning products, assessment services, English language learning solutions, professional certification and licensure testing, and workforce skills solutions to education institutions, government bodies, employers, professionals and individual learners.

Workera operates an AI-powered skills intelligence platform and provides skills assessment to enterprise customers. Pursuant to an Agreement and Plan of Merger, a newly formed, wholly-owned subsidiary of NCS Pearson will merge with and into Workera, with Workera surviving the merger and continuing as a wholly owned subsidiary of NCS Pearson.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
publicly available information, and had regard to the factors in
section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition and Consumer Act 2010
(Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application and currently
before it, the ACCC considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give
rise to any material lessening of competition given:
a. there is a small horizontal overlap between Pearson and
Workera in the supply of digital workforce skills solutions in
Australia, with the parties largely focussing on different
services and customers in Australia
b. Workera has a small presence in Australia
c. there are alternative suppliers of digital workforce skills
solutions in Australia
d. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
or conglomerate effects resulting from exclusionary
conduct, bundling or tying of products post-acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
